identificationModule.briefTitle: Segmentectomy for Ground Glass-dominant Invasive Lung Cancer (ECTOP-1012)
identificationModule.officialTitle: Segmentectomy for Ground Glass-dominant Invasive Lung Cancer With Size of 2-3cm: a Single-arm, Multi-center, Phase III Trial

armGroups.label: Segmentectomy
armGroups.description: Segmentectomy is performed for ground glass-dominant invasive lung cancer with size of 2-3cm.

interventions.name: Segmentectomy
interventions.description: The lungs are divided into multiple lobes. A segmentectomy involves the removal of part of one of the lobes of the lung to entirely remove a cancerous tumor. segmentectomy can preserve more normal functional lung tissues.

primaryOutcomes.description: The event is defined as the tumor recurrence or the death due to any causes.

secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Half year and one year after surgical resection

secondaryOutcomes.description: The event is defined as death due to any causes or last follow-up.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: The site of tumor recurrence and metastasis
secondaryOutcomes.description: Outpatient follow-up was conducted regularly after surgery, and the recurrence or metastasis site and time will be recorded.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From date of surgery to the last follow-up or date of death from any cause, whichever came first, assessed up to 5 years.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Proportion of patients who complete planned segmentectomy.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From the beginning of the surgery to the end of the surgery.

secondaryOutcomes.description: According to the postoperative pathology report of the patients, the proportion of patients with no residual tumor after radical segmentectomy accounted for all patients who underwent segmentectomy.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From surgery to the release of the final pathology report, an average of two weeks.

secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From surgery to patient discharge or 30 days after surgery.
